searchText: Great work! I haven't checked it for missed opcodes yet. A couple of things. Block number will probably stay inside of Eth1 block, likewise timestamp. Regarding `COINBASE` it would probably make sense to pass proposer's address to eth1-engine, so it could be included into a block as coinbase. Because coinbase will likely be used to pay transaction fees on Eth1 Shard. Coinbase and friends are currently part of the eth1 engine configuration. Likewise, no need to pass the list of blockhashes by rpc, the engine is aware of them. One thought regarding the difficulty: if it is indeed used as a rng seed, then maybe it should be _random_ (based on some consensus variable) in order to make sure that this stuff doesn't break > Great work! Regarding `COINBASE` it would probably make sense to pass proposer's address to eth1-engine, so it could be included into a block as coinbase. Because coinbase will likely be used to pay transaction fees on Eth1 Shard. <@!425572898787426305> wdym 'stay inside' eth1 block? does the eth1-engine have some notion of block/timestamp independent of the eth2-client? > One thought regarding the difficulty: if it is indeed used as a rng seed, then maybe it should be _random_ (based on some consensus variable) in order to make sure that this stuff doesn't break <@!353136597522448385> one argument against is that it's not as intuitive a definition for applications that try to use it down the road and is bound to lead to confusion (relative to difficulty = 0, which qualitatively makes sense)
